title: Rezk diagonal sharpness for equifibered simplicial diagrams
statement: Use small simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the Kan--Quillen model structure from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. A commutative square is homotopy cartesian when its upper-left corner maps by a weak homotopy equivalence to the homotopy pullback of the other three corners; for non-Kan objects this is computed after functorial fibrant replacement of the diagram. Call a map $g:E\to B$ sharp if every strict pullback square along every small simplicial map $A\to B$ is homotopy cartesian. Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be simplicial diagrams and $p:X\to Y$ a natural transformation. Suppose each $p_m:X_m\to Y_m$ is sharp and every naturality square for an operator $[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$ is homotopy cartesian. Put $(\operatorname{diag}Z)_q=(Z_q)_q$ for $Z=X,Y$, with both operators applied simultaneously. Then $\operatorname{diag}p$ is sharp. Neither the rows nor the diagonals are required to be Kan, and no Reedy fibrancy is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 6.1, printed pp. 11-12; Proposition 2.7, printed p. 4, identifies the definition of sharpness with universal homotopy-cartesianness. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Set $C_nZ=Z_n\times\Delta^n$, $B_nZ=Z_n\times\partial\Delta^n$, and let $L_nZ\subset Z_n$ be the union of the images of the proper horizontal degeneracies. Define $F_nZ\subset\operatorname{diag}Z$ in degree $q$ as the union of the images of $(Z_k)_q\times\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([q],[k])$ for $k\le n$, by $(z,\alpha)\mapsto Z(\alpha)(z)$. The unique horizontal nondegenerate decomposition from [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], applied separately at every vertical degree, gives $F_0Z=Z_0$, inclusions $F_{n-1}Z\subset F_nZ$, and union $\bigcup_nF_nZ=\operatorname{diag}Z$. For $n\ge1$, put $D_nZ=L_nZ\times\Delta^n$, $I_nZ=L_nZ\times\partial\Delta^n$, and $A_nZ=B_nZ\amalg_{I_nZ}D_nZ\subset C_nZ$. There is a pushout $F_nZ=F_{n-1}Z\amalg_{A_nZ}C_nZ$. Indeed a pair $(z,\alpha)$ with nonsurjective $\alpha$ is represented in a lower horizontal degree; a horizontally degenerate $z$ is represented through its degeneracy ancestor. These are exactly $B_nZ$ and $D_nZ$. Outside their union, $z$ is horizontally nondegenerate and $\alpha$ is surjective, and uniqueness of its ancestor identifies no two remaining pairs. This verifies the pushout degreewise and is compatible with vertical operators. All displayed subobject maps are monomorphisms.

source.place: Equation (6.2) and Section 6.7; explicit degreewise nondegenerate-decomposition verification

proof.text: Use the relative-cocone clause of [lem-coef-sharp-special-colimit-gluing] in the following explicit form. For any of its three diagram shapes, a compatible cocone $U_i\to E$ over $V_i\to H$, with $E\to H$ sharp and each component cocone square homotopy cartesian, induces a homotopy-cartesian colimit square. This applies to the finite degeneracy cubes, finite face diagrams and the two spans below: each time the diagram's cofibrancy or monomorphic-leg condition, its sharp components, and both its internal and cocone squares are checked before applying the clause. The target sharp map is specified separately on each use; it is either $p_n$, a product of $p_n$, or an already constructed $F_{n-1}X\to F_{n-1}Y$. Thus no general model-localization theorem, and no result whose dependencies run through this diagonal theorem, is needed.

source.place: Proposition 8.1 with its relative-cocone consequence from finite and sequential cofibrant colimit invariance; see the new lemma statement

proof.text: Induct on $n$ with the strengthened assertion: $F_nX\to F_nY$ is sharp, and the square $C_kX\to F_nX$ over $C_kY\to F_nY$ is homotopy cartesian for every $0\le k\le n$. For $n=0$ this is the hypothesis on $p_0$ and the identity square, since $\Delta^0$ is terminal. By [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus], every product $p_k\times\mathrm{id}_K$ is sharp; each original operator square stays homotopy cartesian after multiplying by any $K$; and the square changing only the factor $K\to K'$ is homotopy cartesian. These facts will verify the vertical sharpness and operator-square hypotheses in the induction step.

source.place: Section 6.7, strengthened induction keeping the comparison squares

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, describe $L_nZ$ by the finite proper-subset diagram indexed by $T\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its value is $Z_{|T|}$, mapped to $Z_n$ by the surjection $\sigma_T:[n]\to[|T|]$, $\sigma_T(j)=|\{t\in T:t\le j\}|$. For $T\subset T'$ let $\rho_{T,T'}:[|T'|]\to[|T|]$ be the unique surjection satisfying $\sigma_T=\rho_{T,T'}\sigma_{T'}$; the transition is $Z(\rho_{T,T'}):Z_{|T|}\to Z_{|T'|}$. Each $\sigma_T$ has an increasing section, so its degeneracy map is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] at each vertical degree: if $z=Z(\tau)y$ is its unique expression with $y$ horizontally nondegenerate, let $J=\{j:\tau(j-1)<\tau(j)\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Then $z$ lies in the $T$-image exactly when $J\subseteq T$, since this is exactly the condition that $\tau$ factor through $\sigma_T$. Thus the $T$-image intersects the $T'$-image in the $(T\cap T')$-image. Every equality of representatives in two images is therefore already identified through their intersection object. The colimit is their union $L_nZ$, and the latching map at $T$ is the injective inclusion of the union of its proper-subset images into its $T$-image. This proves precisely the cofibrancy required by [lem-coef-sharp-special-colimit-gluing](3), also after taking a product with a fixed $K$. All naturality squares are the hypothesized operator squares, or their products, so that lemma makes $L_nX\to L_nY$ sharp. The step-2 cocone argument to the sharp $p_n$, using the original degeneracy squares, shows $L_nX\to X_n$ over $L_nY\to Y_n$ homotopy cartesian. In particular $D_nX\to C_nX$ and $I_nX\to B_nX$ over their $Y$ counterparts are homotopy cartesian by [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus].

source.place: Section 6.7, latching proper-subset diagram and Proposition 8.1(3)

proof.text: Assume the induction assertion for $n-1$. For each proper nonempty subset $T\subsetneq[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, put $k=|T|-1$. The map $X_n\times\Delta^T\to F_{n-1}X$ factors through $X_k\times\Delta^k$: first restrict by the increasing face $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, identifying $\Delta^T$ with $\Delta^k$, and then use the $k$th cell cocone. Its square over $Y$ is homotopy cartesian by the product operator square, the induction assertion and pasting from [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus]. At $T=\varnothing$ the source and base are empty, so the same assertion is immediate from the strict-pullback criterion. The proper-face diagram $T\mapsto X_n\times\Delta^T$ has colimit $B_nX$ and is cofibrant: its latching maps are boundary-face union inclusions. Its values and transition squares are sharp and homotopy cartesian because all are base changes of $p_n$. Apply the step-2 finite-subset cocone argument to the sharp target $F_{n-1}X\to F_{n-1}Y$. It gives the homotopy-cartesian square $B_nX\to F_{n-1}X$ over $B_nY\to F_{n-1}Y$.

source.place: Section 6.7, boundary attachment squares; expanded proper-face argument

proof.text: For each proper $T\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with $k=|T|<n$, the map $X_k\times\Delta^n\to F_{n-1}X$ factors as $X_k\times\Delta^n\to X_k\times\Delta^k\to F_{n-1}X$, the first map using $\Delta(\sigma_T):\Delta^n\to\Delta^k$. Write $c_k:C_kZ\to F_{n-1}Z$ for the cell cocone. For $T\subset T'$ the transition is $Z(\rho_{T,T'})\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}$. In vertical degree $q$, the $T$-cocone sends $(z,\alpha:[q]\to[n])$ to $Z(\sigma_T\alpha)(z)$. The $T'$-cocone of its image is $Z(\sigma_{T'}\alpha)Z(\rho_{T,T'})(z)=Z(\rho_{T,T'}\sigma_{T'}\alpha)(z)=Z(\sigma_T\alpha)(z)$. This proves cocone compatibility, including every multiple inclusion, and the construction commutes with vertical operators because the two simplicial directions commute. The first square over $Y$ is a strict pullback of the sharp product $p_k\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^k}$; the second is homotopy cartesian by induction. Pasting in [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus] and the step-2 proper-subset cocone argument therefore give $D_nX\to F_{n-1}X$ over $D_nY\to F_{n-1}Y$ homotopy cartesian. The vertical maps on $B_n,D_n,I_n,C_n$ are sharp, since they are products of $p_n$ or of the sharp latching map from step 4. The square $I_nX\to D_nX$ over $I_nY\to D_nY$ is a strict pullback of the latter sharp map, hence homotopy cartesian. The square $I_n\to B_n$ is homotopy cartesian by step 4. Thus the intersection cocones to both $C_n$ and $F_{n-1}$ have homotopy-cartesian squares by pasting.

source.place: Section 6.7, degenerate attachment and intersection squares

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-sharp-special-colimit-gluing](2) to the span $B_nZ\leftarrow I_nZ\to D_nZ$ for $Z=X,Y$. Both legs are inclusions, the vertical maps are sharp and both naturality squares are homotopy cartesian by steps 4-6. Its pushout $A_nX\to A_nY$ is sharp. Apply the step-2 span cocone argument twice: to $C_nX\to C_nY$ using $B_n\to C_n$ (a strict product pullback), $D_n\to C_n$ (step 4), and their intersection; and to $F_{n-1}X\to F_{n-1}Y$ using steps 5-6. This gives homotopy-cartesian squares on both arrows $A_n\to C_n$ and $A_n\to F_{n-1}$. All sharpness and product-pullback assertions used here are given by [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus].

source.place: Section 6.7, first pushout application of Proposition 8.1(2)

proof.text: Now apply [lem-coef-sharp-special-colimit-gluing](2) to $F_{n-1}Z\leftarrow A_nZ\hookrightarrow C_nZ$. The right leg is mono by step 1; the vertical maps are sharp by induction and step 7; the two naturality squares are homotopy cartesian by step 7. Thus the pushout $F_nX\to F_nY$ is sharp, and its cocone squares from $F_{n-1}$ and $C_n$ are homotopy cartesian. For $k<n$, paste the inductively known square $C_k\to F_{n-1}$ with $F_{n-1}\to F_n$, using [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus]; this retains every old cell square. The new cell square is already supplied by the gluing lemma. This completes the strengthened induction.

source.place: Section 6.7, second pushout application of Proposition 8.1(2)

proof.text: The sequences $F_0Z\subset F_1Z\subset\cdots$ have monomorphic transition maps, sharp vertical maps and homotopy-cartesian naturality squares for successive arrows by step 8. All longer-arrow squares are homotopy cartesian by repeated pasting in [lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus]. Apply [lem-coef-sharp-special-colimit-gluing](1). It makes $\operatorname{colim}_nF_nX\to\operatorname{colim}_nF_nY$ sharp. These colimits are literally the diagonals by step 1, so this is the required $\operatorname{diag}p$. The argument used monomorphisms and sharp maps throughout and imposed no Kan or Reedy-fibrancy condition.

source.place: Section 6.7, final sequential-union application of Proposition 8.1(1)
